title: Surrogate McKenna West’s baby in critical condition after heart surgery
text:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

The baby at the center of a multi-state legal fight after the surrogate mother refused to terminate her pregnancy is in critical condition following complex heart surgery, the boy’s biological parents claimed.

Nasheen Gilkar and Omar Ahmed, who are battling surrogate McKenna West over custody of the boy, claimed the baby underwent the open-heart surgery  known as the Norwood Procedure, TMZ reported.

Over the last 24 hours, “Serious medical developments have arisen that impact the health and safety of the child. The child is in critical condition and being closely monitored at the hospital,” Gilkar and Ahmed said, according to court documents.

The parents claim that the baby, who they named Rumi, has seen his condition decline “significantly” after suffering potential complications from the procedure.

Gilkar and Ahmed are currently suing West, a 28-year-old nurse from Alaska, for more than $100,000 for keeping the baby rather than aborting it as she agreed, according to the lawsuit.

Under the contract, West recieved $60,000 to carry their child, which included an “abortion clause” allowing termination if there were birth defects.

At around 20 weeks, the unborn child was diagnosed with hypoplastic left heart syndrome, a life-threatening medical condition.

West, however, refused their request to abort it, and instead traveled to Texas, where she would be recognized as the birth mother under state law.

The baby was born on Aug. 12 and West named him Gabriel — but the biological parents insist his name is Rumi.

Gilkar and Ahmed have demanded more than $100,000 in damages from McKenna for breaking the deal plus unspecified damages for her alleged “malicious, outrageous conduct.”

West’s decision to keep the baby ignited a national conversation on abortion and surrogacy as it now involves courts and officials in three different states.

Gilkar and Ahmed “haven’t given [West] anything” since she declined to terminate the pregnancy, Lincoln Wilson, an attorney for West, told The Post.

The mother is preparing an all-out legal battle to become Gabriel’s legal parent.

“She is seeking parentage of the child because she gave birth in Texas, and in Texas, if you give birth to a child, it’s your child,” Wilson said.
